headline_marked: [[PM Tarique Rahman to visit Chattogram puja mandap]] today for Durga Puja greetings
headline: PM Tarique Rahman to visit Chattogram puja mandap today for Durga Puja greetings
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will exchange Durga Puja greetings with the Hindu community at JM Sen Hall in Chattogram. Security has been significantly heightened for the visit, with extensive preparations underway.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to visit the JM Sen Hall puja mandap in Chattogram’s Rahmatganj this evening. He will exchange Durga Puja greetings with members of the Hindu community during his visit.

Ahead of the visit, security has been significantly stepped up across the area. Officials from the district administration and law enforcement agencies have been inspecting arrangements since Monday morning to ensure a peaceful event.

Chattogram Deputy Commissioner Jahidul Islam Mia held discussions with Puja Udjapan Parishad leaders yesterday regarding preparations. Roads in key areas like Kazir Dewri, Jamal Khan, Rahmatganj, and Anderkilla have been cleaned, dividers repainted, and unauthorized posters removed.

Eviction drives have also cleared illegal makeshift shops from footpaths to ensure smooth passage and enhance security. Prof Arpan Kanti Banerjee, acting president of the Chattogram City Puja Udjapan Parishad, expressed delight over the Prime Minister's visit.

Due to space constraints inside the mandap, a maximum of 300 designated guests will be permitted for security reasons. Chattogram Metropolitan Police Commissioner Hasan Md Shawkat Ali confirmed that police and plainclothes officers have been deployed round-the-clock, coordinating closely with organizers.

headline_marked: [[Dengue death toll reaches 352]] as 4 more die in 24 hours
headline: Dengue death toll reaches 352 as 4 more die in 24 hours
summary: Bangladesh's dengue crisis deepens with 1,851 new hospitalizations and four more deaths in the last 24 hours, bringing the total fatalities this year to 352, according to the DGHS.
details: Bangladesh has reported four more dengue fatalities and 1,851 new hospitalizations in the last 24 hours. These latest figures, released on Monday by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), push the total death toll this year to 352.

Of the recent deaths, two occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, one in Dhaka North City Corporation, and one outside Mymensingh City Corporation. This highlights the widespread impact of the disease across different regions.

Among the newly admitted patients, 148 were hospitalized in Dhaka North and 231 in Dhaka South. An additional 363 patients were admitted to hospitals elsewhere in Dhaka Division, indicating a significant burden on the capital's healthcare system.

Other divisions also reported substantial new admissions: Khulna Division with 253, Rajshahi with 233, Chattogram with 220, and Barishal with 192. Mymensingh saw 92 new patients, Rangpur 93, and Sylhet 26, showing the national reach of the outbreak.

The DGHS also reported that 1,839 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals within the past 24 hours. This brings the total number of dengue patients admitted nationwide this year to 114,251, with 107,865 having recovered and returned home.

The current year's outbreak is particularly severe, with the DGHS bulletin noting that 2023 marked the worst recorded level since 2000. In 2023, 321,179 people were hospitalized and 1,705 died from dengue.

Last year, more than 400 people succumbed to dengue, and approximately 102,000 cases were recorded. These escalating figures underscore the ongoing challenge Bangladesh faces in controlling the spread of the disease.
